target_customer: Construction projects and contractors in London that hire temporary workers
problem: Contractors pay high agency fees and workers wait for pay. BuildStream handled recruitment and payroll for temporary construction labour, claiming clients save 35 percent on agency fees.
business_model: Marketplace and payroll take rate on temporary labour

founders.name: Terry Clarke
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him under former founders; no background given.

founders.name: David Polonski
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him under former founders; no background given.

competitors.name: TempaGoGo
competitors.what: Online marketplace of vetted recruitment agencies for temporary construction staff
competitors.traction_then: More than 100 vetted agencies on the platform

technical_complexity.rationale: A staffing marketplace with payroll is standard web engineering; the hard parts are UK payroll and compliance rules.

defensibility.rationale: Staffing agencies and other marketplaces serve the same workers; the main risk is workers and contractors going direct.

market_need_then: The company's own page claims clients save 35 percent on agency fees; a 2019 trade press piece covered a competing temp marketplace, indicating attention to the problem.

brand_strength.rationale: A brand search returned only directory pages and unrelated results; the name is generic for construction software.

outcome_analysis: BuildStream, a London construction labour and payroll marketplace from the Summer 2019 batch, is listed by YC as inactive with both founders under former founders. One database reports a $1.7M seed in January 2022 and $2.56M over eight rounds, but no shutdown note or post-mortem was found, so the cause of the failure is not public and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: The 2022 seed rests on a single database (CB Insights, also echoed by VCBacked). CB Insights total of $2.56M over 8 rounds exceeds the one recorded round, so earlier rounds are missing and not found. A search snippet said it raised over $700K from Y Combinator, Urban US and Plug and Play; the page was not opened and is not recorded as a round. StartupIntros lists $12M seed in October 2021, which I judge unreliable and did not record. Construction payroll company Trayd is a different company. Competitor list has one dated source only.
